1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% if sentiment is positive or neutral.

2. After a sharp price spike (e.g., >95), model tends to overshoot and continue upward — cap forecast growth rate to 1–2% per day post-spike unless sentiment is strongly bullish.

3. When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.0), model often fails to adjust downward — apply a downward bias of 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is negative or volatile.

4. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price is above 95 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should trend downward slightly (e.g., -0.5% per day) unless sentiment is strongly bullish.

5. Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if true outcome shows a sharp drop after day 10–15, adjust forecast to reflect earlier correction — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day after day 10.

6. If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22 or -0.61), model tends to ignore them — apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% for each negative sentiment value > -0.2.

7. Model underestimates price drops after a spike — if true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, forecast should be adjusted downward by 2–4% for the next 3–5 days, regardless of sentiment.
